_why: SPEC-207. The crawl on/off state used to live only in Supabase edge secrets — invisible in git, unreviewable, and unanswerable from the sandbox. Whether we were crawling was a question nobody could answer without opening a dashboard. It lives here now: committed, diffable, and reversible with one PR. CI pushes these into the edge-function runtime on every change.
_founder: 2026-08-03: 'add all sources not just creators to the crawl at 100 leads each max to review (except yelp)'. Supersedes 2026-08-02 'activate the crawls just for the creator sources to get 100 of each then pause alongside the rest to audit' — the creator-only phase is over; the audit-then-clear shape stays.
_CRAWLS_SUSPENDED: Global stop. false = the allowlist below decides. Defaults to SUSPENDED in code, so a typo here fails closed.
_CRAWLS_ONLY: ONLY these sources may run. SPEC-243 (founder, 2026-08-03, verbatim: 'add all sources not just creators to the crawl at 100 leads each max to review (except yelp)') — the FULL rota minus yelp. Every source here is governed by a stop: the two creator sources (ig_services via ig-scraper-user-search, se:web-harvest via creator-harvest — SPEC-230: exactly TWO, both listed or the last path to a founder target silently closes) self-stop at CREATOR_TARGET, and every services source self-stops at SOURCE_AUDIT_CAP leads (below). se:web-harvest is not in the crawl rota (cron-driven, SPEC-237), but creator-harvest reads this allowlist and refuses to run when its name is absent. ig-creator-marketplace stays REMOVED (SPEC-221). yelp is PAUSED as a source, not deleted (founder, 2026-08-02: 'don't delete yelp.. just pause as a source') — it stays in the code and the dashboards, its rows are kept, and it stays out of this allowlist until the founder re-activates it (gate #239).
_CREATOR_TARGET: EACH creator source stops ITSELF at this count — founder, 2026-08-02: 'get 100 of each then pause alongside the rest to audit.' ig_services counts eq(discovered_via, ig-scraper-user-search); creator-harvest counts by PREFIX like(discovered_via, se:web-harvest%) because its tag is stamped per run day (SPEC-237). Checked before any job is claimed / any search is fired, so neither can overshoot while nobody is watching.
_PHASE1_CITY_QUOTA: SET BY THE FOUNDER — a FORMULA, not a number (2026-08-02, verbatim: '50k services for nyc (with 5% of that as creators).. adjusting each city based on relative size of dma (eg: if miami is 10% of new it should be 5k services and 250 creators..'). services(city) = 50,000 × DMA(city)/DMA(NYC), DMA size in Nielsen TV households (2024-25 LTMUE), rounded to the nearest 100; creators = 5% of that (informational here — CREATOR_TARGET=100 is the standing get-100-then-audit order and governs creators until the founder lifts it). SPEC-244 (founder, 2026-08-03: 'THE DMA is technically held by it's own DMA definition (that's unrelated to state)... use a standard DMA definition / boundary'): keys are Nielsen DMA codes, never state abbreviations — 501 = New York (7,494,510 households → 50,000), 528 = Miami-Ft. Lauderdale (1,756,920, 23.4% → 11,700). A state is not a DMA: Florida holds multiple DMAs (Miami-Ft. Lauderdale, Orlando, Tampa) and the New York DMA reaches into NJ (Jersey City, Newark) and CT. Phase 2 quotas are PRE-COMPUTED in the build spec (LA 38,900 · Chicago 24,400 · Dallas 21,800 · Philadelphia 21,000 · Houston 18,700 · Atlanta 18,400 · DC 17,600 · Boston 17,200 · Phoenix 14,700; 9th metro = Boston, founder 2026-08-02) but stay OUT of this map until Phase 1 is full — a DMA absent from the map cannot be crawled past phase gating. Both consumers (fulfill-crawl, _growth-scope.mjs) parse this map FAIL-CLOSED: empty, unparseable, or non-positive values mean Phase 2 stays locked. Refresh the numbers when Nielsen publishes new estimates.
_SOURCE_AUDIT_CAP: SPEC-243 (founder, 2026-08-03, verbatim: 'add all sources not just creators to the crawl at 100 leads each max to review (except yelp)'). EACH services source stops ITSELF at this many leads_services rows — counted per source BEFORE any job is claimed in fulfill-crawl, the same shape as CREATOR_TARGET, because a target that depends on someone watching a dashboard is how a $1 tranche became $108. The count uses every data_source value a source's rows actually carry (AUDIT_CAP_SOURCES in _shared/opsPayload.ts — yellowpages_apify writes 'yellowpages', google_lsa's history includes folded 'google_sponsored' rows; counting only the rota name reads 0 beside real rows, the Part-6 two-names defect). Unreadable count = that source refuses to run (fail closed — refusing costs nothing). Sources already past the cap pause immediately: their 100-to-review already exists in sample-100-<source>.csv. When every source is capped, everything is paused and the founder audits the exports, then names cleared sources. Spend rules unchanged: the $1 tranche ladder and $0.05/lead cap still gate every paid source underneath this.
_CONTACT_BAR_PCT: A source under 40% contactable is PARKED, not retried (founder, 2026-08-02).
